The chain order was chosen to reproduce the target's store order exactly (innermost assignment emits first, so Z-then-X and Time-then-Value-then-CurValue). 8 words, aligned view over 0x60:0x84 BYTE-IDENTICAL to HEAD. (4) INLINED HELPER: `static void SetAmbientSpecial(f32 time, f32 value) { AmbientSpecialTime = time; AmbientSpecialValue = value; AmbientSpecialCurValue = value; }` called as `SetAmbientSpecial(sLightingZero, sLightingZero);`. The name is not invented - LIGHTS.OBJ in the Xbox PDB carries a real `SetAmbientSpecial` (offset 298704, size 48) three source positions above InitLighting, so this was the most plausible reconstruction of the tail. REGRESSED 8 -> 13 words at 38/38: the tail block stayed exactly as it was (the 0x60:0x84 aligned view is unchanged) and five NEW differing words appeared EARLIER in the function, so the helper's presence perturbed the prologue-side allocation without touching the residual it was aimed at. attributes.residual: The rule stays; this record is the source-exhaustion provenance it did not have, and it retires the 2026-08-29 prose park it supersedes (which recorded 'bounded source-shape matrix' with no probed_form at all). THE MECHANISM, from the aligned raw view. The function is byte-identical to retail for its first 25 instructions and diverges only in the eight-word tail after `bl DoLighting`. Two .sdata2 constants are hoisted to the top of that block in BOTH streams, in the SAME emission order - +0x64 loads @sLightingZero, +0x68 loads @sNegativeHalf - and BOTH streams then issue the same six stores in the same order. The entire residual is which of the two loads takes f0: retail puts sLightingZero in f0 and sNegativeHalf in f1, we put sLightingZero in f1 and sNegativeHalf in f0, and the six stores follow. What this pass establishes that the previous park did not: the assignment is INVARIANT under every source-level handle on web creation. Three forms that change how and in what order the two webs come into existence - a chained assignment, a named local for one constant, and a named local for the OTHER constant, which inverts the source creation order outright - all compile to BYTE-IDENTICAL code. The one form that did change the block's shape (an inlined helper) regressed. So the f0/f1 choice here is not reachable through statement form, temp identity, or creation order, and any remaining source lever has to work through what else is live in the block, not through how the two constants are spelled.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Compare this function's tail block against fn_80051480's pre-loop block, where the SAME question was measured on a different TU. If retail there gives f0 to a LOW-use web, the use-count reading is wrong. Measured 2026-09-03: retail gives f0 to fn_80051480's `best_dist` accumulator, which has THREE uses against the loop scratch's nine, so the use-count reading is ALREADY CONTRADICTED as a general rule and survives here only as a local tie-break. Treat it as the weakest of the untried axes.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes - the two load registers, all six store registers and their offsets were read from the aligned raw view against the retail bytes over the whole 38-instruction body, and the four-versus-two use counts were counted in both streams.
hypothesis.statement: The remaining lever is NOT on the two constants' source order, identity, or assignment form - all three are measured inert - but on what ELSE is live in the tail block. Retail gives f0 to the web with FOUR uses (sLightingZero: ScratchY, Time, Value, CurValue) and f1 to the web with TWO (sNegativeHalf: ScratchZ, ScratchX); ours gives f0 to the two-use web. The untried axis is therefore a USE-COUNT axis: add or remove a use of one constant inside the block (for instance by writing one of the six stores through a different constant that happens to hold the same value, or by splitting one store out of the block) and read whether the f0 assignment follows the use count. Any such form must be checked against 38/38 first, because the two forms tried here that changed the block's shape at all (the inlined helper) cost words.
